title: Technology Sector Update for 09/24/2018: JKS,TEUM,SYMC,MU
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT +0.43%
AAPL +1.35%
IBM -0.81%
CSCO -0.22%
GOOG +0.58%
Technology stocks managed to pad their slim earlier gains, rising over 0.4% late in Monday trading while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index posted a nearly 0.4% increase, reversing a small mid-day decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) JinkoSolar ( JKS ) was back near its Monday session low, falling over 2%, with the photovoltaic-panels company receiving little apparent help from an announcement it was partnering with Edisun Microgrids to develop a high-performance rooftop bundle for commercial and industrial customers. The new Eagle PowerTrack bundle will feature JinkoSolar's Eagle G2 modules and Edisun's PV Booster and are expected to deliver 30% more energy per panel and resulting in significantly lower levelized cost of electricity and boosting the return on investment over traditional systems. Financial terms of the new partnership were not disclosed.
In other sector news:
(+) Pareteum ( TEUM ) was almost 7% higher Monday afternoon, easing somewhat from a more than 11% gain earlier in the session that followed the cloud services company said it received a five-year contract worth an estimated $38 million from an unnamed internet of things and mobile virtual network company. Under the terms of the deal, Pareteum will support the customer's business expansion in southern Asia, including plans to add WiFi, Blockchain, M2M, and Smart City capabilities.
(+) Symantec ( SYMC ) still was more than 3% higher Monday afternoon, giving back a portion of its 6% gain soon after the opening bell that followed the cyber-security software firm saying it has finished an internal examination and has concluded there is no need for any additional adjustments or restatements of its recent quarterly financial results. The company began the probe by the board's audit committee after an employee alleged there were problems with its accounting practices
(+) Micron Technology ( MU ) advanced Monday, rising almost 2%, despite analysts at Needham & Co cutting their price target for the DRAM memory company by $20 to $80 a share. The brokerage also reiterated its Strong Buy rating for the stock.
